Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates a model’s ability to solve real software engineering issues by generating patches that make a repository’s tests pass, using problems that have been human-verified as solvable. It emphasizes end-to-end bug fixing under realistic repo constraints rather than isolated coding puzzles.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Decision-making (minor)
L3:

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends SWE-bench-style tasks beyond Python to multiple programming languages, testing whether a model can transfer debugging and patching skills across language ecosystems. It stresses generalization to different tooling, idioms, and libraries while retaining end-to-end repository reasoning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a harder, larger-scale software engineering benchmark intended to be more challenging and more robust to contamination, with tasks spanning multiple languages and more complex codebases. It probes whether models can reliably execute longer debugging/implementation trajectories under realistic constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility, Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agentic performance in command-line environments, where a model must execute shell commands, manipulate files, and iterate based on program outputs. It measures tool-using autonomy, error recovery, and maintaining task state over multi-step terminal workflows.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Attention (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: BrowseComp assesses deep-research style question answering using browsing/search tools, requiring models to find, verify, and synthesize information from documents. It emphasizes reliable information gathering and citation-quality synthesis rather than closed-book recall.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Planning, Attention, Working Memory
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: τ2-bench evaluates tool-using agents in multi-turn, policy-constrained customer-service scenarios (e.g., retail, airline, telecom) with simulated users and APIs. It focuses on following domain policies while coordinating dialog, tool calls, and error handling over extended interactions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension, Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control, Empathy (minor)

Description: OSWorld benchmarks multimodal computer-use agents on real OS/application tasks (e.g., navigation, form filling, configuration) under step limits. It requires perception of GUIs, selecting actions like clicks/typing, and adapting to interface state changes across many steps.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a “fluid reasoning” benchmark of abstract grid transformations where models infer latent rules from few input-output examples and produce correct outputs for new inputs. It is designed to reduce reliance on memorized knowledge and emphasize novel pattern induction and generalization.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Spatial Representation & Mapping, Planning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon autonomous decision-making in a simulated vending machine business over many steps, including procurement, pricing, inventory, and negotiation-like interactions. It measures sustained coherence, goal pursuit, and adaptation to changing market conditions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Reward Mechanisms, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas measures real-world tool use through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), requiring models to discover tools, call APIs correctly, handle errors, and compose multi-step workflows across services. It targets practical tool invocation robustness rather than single-call function selection.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: FinanceAgent evaluates agentic performance on tasks typical of entry-level financial analysts, such as analyzing financial documents, performing calculations, and producing structured deliverables. It stresses multi-step quantitative reasoning, domain knowledge use, and clear reporting.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Decision-making, Planning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition

Description: CyberGym evaluates cybersecurity agent capability on large numbers of tasks involving finding known vulnerabilities and, in some settings, discovering new ones in real software projects. It probes code comprehension, exploit-relevant reasoning, and iterative debugging/verification under realistic constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor), Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SpreadsheetBench tests an agent’s ability to interpret and manipulate spreadsheets (e.g., formulas, tables, transformations) using tool-assisted workflows. It targets structured data reasoning and accurate, stepwise edits that preserve spreadsheet semantics.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning, Attention (minor), Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)

It is designed to test advanced reasoning, knowledge integration, and robustness on hard, long-tail problems.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)

Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GPQA Diamond is a curated subset of GPQA designed to be difficult for non-experts and resistant to simple web lookup, consisting of graduate-level science multiple-choice questions. It targets deep conceptual understanding and multi-step scientific reasoning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor), Decision-making (minor)

Description: MMMLU extends MMLU to multiple languages, evaluating knowledge and reasoning across many academic subjects using multilingual questions. It probes whether a model can preserve competence across languages and culturally varied formulations.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MMMU is a multimodal benchmark requiring models to answer questions that combine text with images (charts, diagrams, photos) across many disciplines. It tests integrating visual evidence with domain knowledge to produce correct answers.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Multisensory Integration, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor)

Cognitive Functions:

L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Attention (minor)
